policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere and ketiv differ only in orthography of the same verb (defective vs plene); ASV 'kneaded it' renders either identically, and no note is mapped to this unit. Base fallback (qere) retained.
ASV 'lifted up his eyes' is plural, matching the qere עֵינָיו; the ketiv עינו reads as singular 'his eye', which the English does not render.
ASV text reads 'Ammihur', the ketiv עמיחור; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Ammihud' explicitly names the qere as the reading not adopted in the text.
